column1: # Morocco, the Ministry of Habous and Islamic Affairs (habous.gov.ma): city tables, checked at the
# city centres, the units' points (Habous's own are unpublished; profiles-tested.md,
# data-maghreb-libya). Africa/Casablanca; the clock column says how each file is read. Standard Asr.
# Habous prints no imsak: the fast begins at its Fajr (F+E).
# - Each off-habous file holds the live month (13 Sep–12 Oct 2026, printed in UTC+0), read by
#   habous-live, and Wayback captures of earlier month pages printed in legal time, read into UTC by
#   habous-archive (see HabousArchiveFormat: a page keeps its own clock, not tzdata's, around
#   Ramadan). habous-archive skips the misdated days: the Laayoune capture of 19 Sep 2020 is dated
#   October from 19 Oct 2020, where its Dhuhr jumps by about 9 min (those days are September's), and
#   two runs on the default page (28–31 Jan 2020 and 1–6 Oct 2021) carry another month's days.
# - The site's default page and the Ramadan 1445 page, filed without a city, are Rabat's: their Dhuhr
#   sits as far after Rabat's transit as Rabat's own page's does (about 5 min).
# - Imilchil (about 2,150 m) has no unit: it checks the edge, the national margin every other place
# Split: fit on the ten cities' live month; held out, every Wayback page (2015–2025), Rabat's
# 2022–2023 days and Ramadan 1445, and Imilchil. The per-city sunrise and Maghrib were then widened
# where the held-out pages asked for more (proof/7d-maghreb-libya.md).
# - 29 more places, read by hand on 6 Oct 2026 from the same live month (13 Sep–12 Oct 2026) before the page
#   turned: the app's own Moroccan cities whose Arabic name is a place on Habous's list (archive/tables/manual/
#   ma-habous/2026-10-06/), each at the app's city point. All but Azrou lie beyond the ten units and check the
#   edge, the national margin most of Morocco takes; Azrou, 14 km from Ifrane, checks Ifrane's unit off its point.
# ma_laayoune_202405.txt and off-habous-casa.txt repeat the round files' days.
